name: East Germany
flagName: Flag of the German Democratic Republic
summary: Black, red and gold horizontal bands with the state emblem of a hammer and compass in a ring of rye. East Germany added the emblem in 1959 to distinguish its flag from West Germany's.
origin: From its founding in 1949, the German Democratic Republic used the same black-red-gold tricolour as West Germany, both claiming the democratic tradition of 1848.

On 1 October 1959 the GDR added its state emblem. West Germany regarded the new flag as a symbol of division; until the détente of the late 1960s it was sometimes removed by West German police, and it was banned at some international sporting events.
The flag ceased to be used when Germany reunified on 3 October 1990.

colors.name: Black
colors.meaning: The black-red-gold of German democratic tradition.

symbols.name: Hammer and compass
symbols.description: A hammer and a pair of compasses in a ring of rye ears tied with a black-red-gold ribbon.
symbols.meaning: The alliance of workers (hammer), the intelligentsia (compass) and farmers (rye).

facts: From 1956 to 1964 East and West Germany competed at the Olympics as a single team under black-red-gold with the Olympic rings.
Protesters in 1989 often cut the emblem out of East German flags, leaving a hole in the middle.
Its emblem echoes the Soviet hammer and sickle, replacing the sickle with a compass.
clues: Black, red and gold bands with a hammer and compass in a wreath of grain.
Protesters in 1989 cut holes in its centre.
For its first ten years it was identical to its western neighbour's flag.
Its emblem stood for workers, intellectuals and farmers.
